surface_verification.justification: No startable surface: the change is confined to a shared Python verifier module (spec_checks.py S9/S10 guard), its guard module docstring, its unit tests and a docs catalog row. Shipwright exposes no web/CLI/API surface that exercises these phase-quality checks outside the pytest suite, which ran green at F0.

behaviors.behavior: S9 SKIPs when the audited run_id has no exact iterate_history entry (sentinel '', 'unknown', 'UNKNOWN') instead of inheriting an unrelated run's category
S10 SKIPs on the same sentinel run_ids
S9/S10 SKIP for a NON-sentinel run_id lacking an exact entry — the case the read-time rollup filter (is_sentinel_run) does not exclude, so it reached the triage backlog
S9/S10 still emit their genuine WARN for a run_id WITH an exact entry — the guard does not over-fire
S9/S10's verdict no longer changes when ONLY an unrelated run's category changes (feature vs chore) on otherwise identical repo state
The work-tree guard still precedes the new run_id guard, so a git fault keeps its own diagnostic rather than being misreported as an audit-context mismatch

The phase-quality Stop-audit seam supplies an id that is never an iterate_history key, for both session-id values the hook can actually emit ('unknown' and a UUID) — pins the accepted consequence so it fails loudly if the seam is repaired

The loop-var branch (SHIPWRIGHT_LOOP_ID + _UNIT_ID, campaign/autonomous runs) yields a NON-sentinel id that survives the rollup filter and still SKIPs — the branch where the pre-fix bogus verdict was actionable
